title: The Relationship between Mushroom Intake and Cognitive Performance: An Epidemiological Study in the European Investigation of Cancer—Norfolk Cohort (EPIC-Norfolk) - PMC
abstract: The objectives of the present study were as follows: (1) to utilize the EPIC-Norfolk multicentre cohort data to evaluate whether habitual consumption of mushrooms changes over time; (2) to assess whether dietary mushroom intake is associated with cognitive performance; and (3) to assess whether any significant relationship between mushroom intake and cognitive performance may be explained (in full or in part) by general fruit and vegetable consumption. Cognitive test scores according to mushroom intake while accounting for fruit intake and vegetable intake (excluding mushrooms) as additional covariates: (**a**) CANTAB-PAL: paired associate learning test, (**b**) SF-MMSE: Mini Mental State Examination—short form, (**c**) PM: Prospective memory test, (**d**) HVLT: Hopkins Verbal Learning Task, (**e**) SF-EMSE: Extended Mental State Examination—short form, (**f**) NART: National Adult Reading Test. * 13.Ba D.M., Gao X., Al-Shaar L., Muscat J.E., Chinchilli V.M., Beelman R.B., Richie J.P. Mushroom intake and depression: A population-based study using data from the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), 2005–2016.
